prompt:
A desktop settings page of a software-factory console, 1440 px wide, shown without browser chrome. Top bar: the project name "demo", a moon-and-sun theme toggle, the user "sebastian", "Log out". Nav row under it: "Board", "Notifications" (the current page), "factory", "costs", "alerts". Page heading: "Notifications".

Section "Connections":
- Telegram, connected: name "Telegram", detail "@sebastian", a quiet "Disconnect" button.
- Discord, not connected: name "Discord", a "Connect" action.

Section "Level per project", caption "The level you set for each project you read, with the default of needs-you where the project pings you, else off."
Four rows, each: project name, its current state, a way to set one of "off", "needs-you", "all":
- demo-app, now "default: needs-you"
- ai-software-factory, now "default: off"
- trading-socially, now "all" (the member's own setting)
- womb-site, now "off" (the member's own setting)
DESIGN DIRECTION "quiet log": everything on the page is a one-line monospaced row, like a log you can act on. Each row starts at the same left edge: a marker glyph, then the thing (venue or project), then its state, then a right-aligned word or action. The page looks like terminal output that has been tamed into a setting.
FIXES from review: every action is a visible bracketed text button, unmistakably clickable: [Connect], [Disconnect], and per project row [off] [needs-you] [all] with the current one marked by a small square lamp before the state word, plus [Save] at the row end. No chevrons and no folded rows; each row shows all of itself. A derived default states itself in the line as "default: needs-you" in dim text; the member's own setting shows the word alone at full strength. All state words start at the same column on every row, all actions at another, on a strict monospaced grid.
THEME: dark. Near-black page background, light text, one cyan accent for current things, amber for needs-you states, hairline borders, quiet.
label: log-fix-dark
